name: Free Sketch
description: A full painting studio. 37 pressure-sensitive brushes on layers with blend modes, clipping masks and alpha lock — exported to PNG, JPEG, Photoshop PSD or OpenRaster.
details:
Free Sketch is a raster painting studio in the tradition of Sketchbook, Procreate and Fresco, built for detailed work. Every brush is a real stamp engine: spacing, pressure-to-size and pressure-to-opacity, taper at both ends, jitter, scatter, rotation that follows the stroke, and paper grain pressed through the whole stroke so going back over it fills the same pits the way graphite does.

The library has 37 brushes in eight sets: HB and 6B pencils, mechanical pencil, charcoal, soft pastel and wax crayon; studio pen, fineliner, brush pen, calligraphy nib, technical pen and dry ink; hard and soft round, oil, gouache, flat acrylic and palette knife; watercolour washes that glaze over each other and pool at their edges; alcohol marker, highlighter and felt tip; airbrushes and spray paint that build up while you hold still; splatter, sparkle, glow, foliage and stipple; and soft, hard and bristle blenders plus a blur brush. Every setting of every brush can be tuned and is remembered, and the eraser and smudge tools each keep their own brush.

Layers work like a professional app's: up to 100 depending on canvas size, 17 blend modes, opacity, visibility, lock, alpha lock and clipping masks, with duplicate, merge down, flatten and drag-to-reorder. Selections (lasso, rectangle and ellipse, with add and subtract) confine painting, fills and transforms. The transform tool moves, scales, rotates and flips a layer or just the selected part of it, and resamples once when you apply, so repeated nudges never soften the image.

Also on board: flood fill with tolerance and edge growth for colouring line art, linear and radial gradients, stroked or filled shapes, vertical, horizontal, quadrant and radial symmetry, hue/saturation, brightness/contrast, colour balance, blur, invert and black & white adjustments, a hue-ring colour picker with HSB and RGB sliders, hex entry, palettes and recent colours, and an eyedropper on Alt.

It takes a pen seriously: pressure with an adjustable curve, the stylus's eraser end switches to the eraser, and palm rejection lets fingers pan while the pen draws. Pinch to zoom and rotate, two-finger tap to undo, three-finger tap to redo, or use the keyboard shortcuts you already know — B, E, S, [ and ], Space to pan, R to rotate, H to mirror the view, Shift-click for straight lines. Undo goes back up to 100 steps.

Artwork is saved on this device as you paint. Export a flattened PNG or JPEG, or keep every layer, blend mode and clipping mask with Photoshop PSD, or OpenRaster for Krita, GIMP and MyPaint.
